To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

our diagnosis method is novel both for not requiring exact behavioral models for activities and for its accuracy improving upon dependency-based methods; it is based on observations obtained from partial executions of a service process and re-executions; it can be solved using state-of-the-art constraint solving technology, and its evaluation demonstrates that it is superior in accuracy to classic dependencybased methods on realistically-sized problems.
our novel diagnosis method is more accurate than existing methods, and that its accuracy can be improved by re-executing parts of the process.

we developed a method for diagnosing failures of orchestrated service process executions that is novel both in the sense that it does not rely on exact behavioral models for activities, and that it yields better accuracy than classic dependency-based methods.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the source(s) of a fault in an orchestrated Web service process execution, given a set of observations obtained from partial executions of the process.
the identification of the source(s) of a fault of a Web service process execution.
the identification of the source(s) of a fault in a service process execution, which is a task that is of growing importance, especially in automated service composition and orchestration scenarios.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the approach is a very promising one and that it should be further evaluated in more realistic settings.
we are not able to make a clear statement about which of the two approaches (dependency-based vs. our approach) is more efficient.
the approach presented here is a promising step towards the development of an efficient and accurate automated diagnosis method that can be applied to service process executions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the proposed method is able to detect faults in service process executions with a high accuracy, while requiring minimal information about the service process and the service behavior, and without requiring the service to be available for execution.
we have developed a novel diagnosis method that is able to diagnose service failures even if the activities are modeled only by a partial knowledge, i.e. a set of partial traces.
we present a method for identifying the source of a service failure that is based on the analysis of a trace.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of partial knowledge about the activities in the process is beneficial for the diagnosis process, and that this knowledge can be used effectively by exploiting the observations from re-executions of the process.
the diagnosis problem can be solved efficiently, and that the accuracy of the method is high, even when the knowledge of the process behavior is partial.
the use of partial knowledge about the behavior of services is a promising avenue to improve diagnosis accuracy.
